items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: I kind of had a little problem with Bill Dixon... But we just had some problems and so I decided it was time to move on.

ctx.x: You were able to stay in music in those ten years though?

Well sort of. I had a pretty checkered history in there. I was at Indiana University and then I went back to Chicago and ended up working in the library — the biomedical library sciences building there for a while. I saved enough money to buy a car, get out of town, ended up in Bennington, Vermont because I had some friends from high school that were there, and ended up accompanying for dance classes. But also I was working at this fast food restaurant. But I ended up being there for about three years and then…

And I came to New York and started playing guitar, continued playing piano accompanying for dance classes, was running an elevator, you know, doing all kinds of odd jobs. By the end of the 70s I was playing five nights a week in this funky little club on the upper west side which is long gone called Clifford’s Lounge.
